text:
Priya: FYI tenant 'globex' just reported account churn: SCIM created new user entries instead of updating existing ones after we shipped the RBAC role flip. Looks like SAML NameID format changed upstream and our externalId derivation failed. Also seeing KMS errors when trying to decrypt stored externalId tokens.

Marcus: Can you paste the minimal logs and the SAML assertion sample?

Priya: Logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-10T09:41:12Z ERROR provisioner: decrypt extid failed: kms.InvalidCiphertextException: ciphertext refers to a different key
  at kms.(*Client).Decrypt
  at provisioner.(*scim).resolveExternalId
2026-03-10T09:41:12Z INFO provisioner: createUser fallback to username because extid decrypt failed -> created duplicate
```
SAML assertion snippet we received: `NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent" > abc123|svc`

Zoe: Two separate problems: 1) SP IdP changed NameID delimiter and we didn't have a robust parser; 2) KMS rekeying happened yesterday and the new key has a policy that grants cross-account access to a partner account (security flag). That could be a vuln surface if partner role is privileged.

Daniel: Do we have the key change event? infra-bot, can you dump the KMS audit for key alias/tenant-extid?

infra-bot: KMS event: 2026-03-10T09:35:00Z Alias update alias/tenant-extid -> keyId=kkk-777; Key policy updated: statement[1].Principal = "arn:aws:iam::999888777:role/partner-sync" (added).

Priya: Ugh adding a partner role to our extid key policy was not intended. That explains the InvalidCiphertextException (rewrap may have used different encryption context). Also need to confirm whether the partner can call ReEncrypt or Decrypt.

Marcus: Immediate mitigations: 1) Pause SCIM provisioning for globex (controlplane toggle); 2) Remove partner principal from key policy and re-add our provisioner role; 3) Run a key rewrap for extids encrypted under the new key back to the verified key.

Zoe: Also we should treat the policy change as a vulnerability -> run a quick blast radius: list tenants using that alias and flag any secrets that may have been re-encrypted. Create incident SEC-2026-043 and notify infra-security pager.

security-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-043 - "Potential extid exposure: KMS policy added external principal + SAML nameid parsing mismatch" https://redwood.incidents/SEC-2026-043

Daniel: Question about rewrap: do we run rewrap via KMS ReEncrypt or do we pull and ReEncrypt client-side? ReEncrypt might log different encryption context which is used in our extid integrity.

Marcus: Use server-side ReEncrypt with EncryptionContext set to {"tenant":"globex","purpose":"extid"} to preserve context. Command (internal): `aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cipher.blob --destination-key-id <canonical-key> --destination-encryption-context '{"tenant":"globex","purpose":"extid"}'` (test with a small batch).

Priya: I'll push a quick patch to the provisioner: compute a fallback externalIdHash from the raw encrypted blob (HMAC of ciphertext) before attempting decrypt so we always emit an audit row (reason=decrypt-failure) and avoid blind create on decrypt errors. PR: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/842 (WIP).

Zoe: For vuln triage: we need timeline and scope. Marcus please produce a list: keyId usage, last 72h ReEncrypt/Decrypt by principal, tenants with alias/tenant-extid mapping. I'll own the attestation and customer notifications.

Marcus: On it. Will run queries and post counts.

infra-bot: Quick query results: 42 Decrypt calls to key kkk-777 between 2026-03-10T09:35:00Z and 2026-03-10T09:45:00Z. Principals: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/provisioner (25 calls), arn:aws:iam::999888777:role/partner-sync (17 calls).

Priya: That 17 calls from partner role is concerning. Zoe, we should offer immediate customer-facing text: "We detected a change in an internal key policy that briefly allowed a partner's sync role to access encrypted tenant identifiers. We have paused provisioning for affected tenants, reverted the key policy, and are rewrapping identifiers. No evidence of data exfiltration so far. We will notify with findings within 24 hours."

Zoe: Approved. Daniel, work with legal on disclosure wording. Marcus, do the policy rollback now and rotate the key. Post rollback output here.

Daniel: Noted. Legal pinged.

Marcus: Rolled back policy at 2026-03-10T09:50:05Z. Command used (sanitized): `aws kms put-key-policy --key-id kkk-777 --policy file://policy-fixed.json`
Policy-fixed.json removed partner principal and ensured arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/provisioner present.

infra-bot: Post-rollback audit: 0 Decrypt calls from partner role after 2026-03-10T09:50:05Z.

Priya: Next steps: 1) Run a safe dry-run rewrap on a sample of 50 extids in staging; 2) Run recon job to dedupe duplicates created during window; 3) Ship audit shim and safe-create guard; 4) Rotate key and force full rewrap. Assignments: Marcus rewrap dry-run + rotation, Priya PR + tests, Zoe customer comms + vuln report, Daniel legal. I'll coordinate with CS to unpause provisioning only after all checks.

Marcus: Dry-run started in staging at 2026-03-10T10:05Z. Using `infractl rewrap-extid --tenant=globex --sample=50 --from-key=kkk-777 --to-key=kkk-555 --preserve-context`

security-bot: Update SEC-2026-043: dry-run success (50/50), recon job queued, audit shim PR opened.

Priya: Thanks. I'll follow up with PR link and smoke test results. If anyone sees further KMS anomalies ping @oncall-bot. :white_check_mark:
